learn.title: Find every angle
learn.body: To solve $\sin x=\frac12$, first find the reference angle with an inverse function, then use the quadrant signs. Between $0$ and $2\pi$ there are usually two answers. Add $2\pi k$ to list them all.

learn.title: Solve $2\cos x-1=0$ on $[0,2\pi)$
steps: Reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$, cosine positive in quadrants I and IV

learn.title: Solve $2\sin^2x-\sin x-1=0$
learn.body: It is a quadratic in $\sin x$.
If the value is outside $[-1,1]$ for sine or cosine, there is no solution.

questions.prompt: How many solutions does $\sin x=0.3$ have on $[0,2\pi)$?
questions.explanation: A value between 0 and 1 is reached once on the way up and once on the way down.
Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, which is 0 at the top and bottom of the circle.

questions.prompt: How many solutions does $\sin x=2$ have?

questions.explanation: Tangent has period $\pi$, so add $\pi$ to $\frac{\pi}{4}$.

questions.prompt: How many solutions does $\sin2x=\frac12$ have on $[0,2\pi)$?
questions.explanation: Doubling the angle doubles the number of cycles, so there are 4 solutions.
Cosine is $-1$ only at the left end of the circle.

questions.prompt: Because sine has period $2\pi$, all solutions come from adding \_\_ to a solution.
questions.explanation: Going once around the circle returns to the same sine.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to its solution on $[0,2\pi)$.
questions.explanation: Check the points on the unit circle.

questions.prompt: Solve $2\cos x-1=0$. Put the steps in order.
steps: List both angles in quadrants I and IV
questions.explanation: Isolate first, then use the circle.
